place.source_title: Lincoln School (originally Germania School), 1000 Tuscola Avenue

brief: Three-storey red-brick neighbourhood school of the early twentieth century, one of Michigan's most intact of its type: a long symmetrical front of banded window groups with stone sills and lintels, a central stone-trimmed entrance pavilion with a small balustraded parapet, a flat roof behind a plain parapet and a raised basement; wide lawns, a corner walk and street trees in a residential neighbourhood.

facade.notes: Lincoln (Germania) School (Saginaw MI, 1917), HABS: a long three-storey red-brick block with grouped classroom windows, a parapet, a small columned entrance porch; set far back on a deep lawn on its own corner block amid frame houses and bare elms

why.note: the 1905-30 graded school: a long symmetrical brick block of classrooms with banded windows for daylight from one side, a central entrance pavilion, a raised basement, on a whole or half block
